ca_magician_the.blurb: The Magician is the biggest spire on the Needles ridge in the southern Sierra, above the Kern River. It holds eleven routes, nearly all trad, with a pair of top-rope problems under the old lookout site. Grades start around 5.7 and cluster at 5.8, with a few climbs in the 5.10s and 5.11s and one 5.12. The long routes are the draw: several run four to ten pitches and finish near the summit, where a lookout once stood. The west face has a few short cracks near its base, while the east face offers quieter slab lines. Expect a remote, high-elevation ridge day with a real walk-in rather than a roadside crag.

ca_purgatory_boulder.blurb: Purgatory Boulder is a single big block at Putah Creek in the Winters area, sitting right at the creek's edge and partly in the water. It is the biggest of the three main boulders on the trail and holds eleven problems. The face toward the road is the steeper one, and the downstream side bulges out. Grades are spread widely, from easy V0 problems through the middle V-grades up to a handful of hard lines near V9. The creek keeps things cooler in summer, but the slope down to it is thick with poison oak, so wear long sleeves and bring a pad.
ca_purgatory_boulder.parking_note: Leave the car in the roadside pullout on the left side of Highway 128, roughly seven miles west of Winters. The boulders are tucked down by the creek and hard to spot from the road.

ca_micro_crag.blurb: Micro Crag is a small but steep roadside cliff in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree, tucked behind a larger formation near the Boy Scout Trail lot. Its eleven routes are all trad, and most are short, crack-focused lines. The grades cover a wide range: a couple of easy climbs, a few in the 5.5 to 5.7 range, and then a harder group of 5.10s and 5.11s that make up the real attraction. It suits climbers who want a quick stop with steep cracks rather than a full day, and the short walk keeps it simple.

ca_bald_rock_dome.blurb: Bald Rock Dome is a tall granite dome in Plumas National Forest near Lake Oroville, rising high above the Middle Fork Feather River canyon. The routes here are long, five or six pitches, and mostly traditional, with a single sport line. Grades run from 5.7 up to the low 5.11s, with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. The climbing has a bold, old-school feel on clean rock, with sparse protection and committing runouts, and the descent from the dome's shoulder involves a gully with rappels. This is a serious day out for experienced parties, not a casual crag.

ca_north_face_5.blurb: The North Face is the first wall you meet on the Hogsback, the smaller formation standing in front of Lover's Leap near Strawberry. All eleven routes are trad, mostly two- and three-pitch climbs. Grades run from 5.5 to the 5.10s, with the greatest number in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, so it works well for newer multi-pitch leaders. The wall sits behind the main cliff and often stays shaded until afternoon, with a talus slope at its base. Climbers walk off to the east after topping out. It is busy with beginners learning the craft.

ca_hot_tub_the.blurb: The Hot Tub is a south-facing formation in the Hidden Valley area of Joshua Tree, just west of the campground and Intersection Rock, on the same block that carries Super Roof. It has eleven routes, mostly trad with two top-rope lines, a mix of cracks and bolted faces. Grades run from 5.8 to the low 5.11s, but most are 5.10, which makes it a good stop for climbers working through that grade. Because it faces south it stays warm on cold days, so plan it for winter mornings rather than a hot afternoon.

ca_missing_link_area_the.blurb: The Missing Link Area is a cluster of hillside boulders on Mount Woodson near Poway, in north San Diego County. Most of the eleven climbs are boulder problems, with a couple of top-rope slabs and one bolt-protected trad line on the largest block. Problems range from VB through V5, plus a few very hard projects, while the roped climbs sit around 5.9 to 5.11. The area is a good place to escape the afternoon sun, but it takes some hiking to reach, and poison oak grows around a few landings, so bring pads and look carefully.
